title: Files & VFS
subsystem_derivation: 03 §4.3 (files — governing custody of information). LAW = namespace, mount, and permission rules; DECISIONS = create / write / link / unlink / permission-change (and `open` itself — the custody grant); CACHE = the directory tree and inode state; STREAM = read-traffic aggregates. Content is never STREAM — every write's payload is full-fidelity to content-addressed blobs, the event records the hash (03 §4.3 [AUDIT-FIX 4]).
activation_note: The files group is the population EP-25 needs; it is implemented and calibrated first (EP-24 §derivation). EP-28 moves the same rows below the syscall line with no row change.

rows.what_it_does: Open (optionally create) a file; return an fd.
rows.conformance_note: The explicit custody grant of §4.3: permission checked, recorded, rule-cited. O_CREAT also records a create decision. The fd-table entry is CACHE. O_EXCL, O_TRUNC, O_APPEND, O_NONBLOCK, and the full errno set (EACCES/EEXIST/ENOENT/EISDIR) identical.
rows.variant_probes_note: openat is driven in the same step list via dir_fd, so §12's ride-the-primary rule is tested rather than assumed for it. openat2 has no stdlib binding and is declared below.
probe_limits: openat2 (and its open_how struct, including RESOLVE_* flags) has no stdlib binding; it rides `open` unproven.
O_NONBLOCK on a FIFO is exercised by files.mknod, not here.

rows.conformance_note: Create + custody grant recorded. Identical to the open equivalent.
probe_limits: creat(2) is driven through its documented equivalent open(2) flag set, which is what the map's own note says it is; the legacy entry point itself is not separately bound.

rows.conformance_note: Symmetric release of the open custody — recorded (low-ceremony). The fd-table slot (CACHE) is dropped. Flush-on-close errors surfaced identically; EBADF matches.

Read-traffic is sampled for the audit aggregate (§4.3), but the caller receives exact bytes — payload is full-fidelity. The offset advance is a CACHE mutation. Short reads, EAGAIN, EINTR semantics identical.
probe_limits: EAGAIN and EINTR are timing-dependent arrival conditions; §11.6 puts timing out of contract and they are not driven.
readv/preadv are not separately bound; they ride `read` unproven.

rows.conformance_note: Content is DECISION-class, never sampled (§4.3 [AUDIT-FIX 4]): payload goes full-fidelity to a content-addressed blob, the write event records the hash. Event granularity may be coalesced under a recorded policy (many small writes → one recorded event citing that policy) — a named calibration, never a silent loss. Short writes, ENOSPC, EDQUOT, O_APPEND atomicity identical.
probe_limits: ENOSPC and EDQUOT need a full or quota-bound filesystem; they are not driven, and a target that cannot report them is not thereby conformant.
pwritev/pwritev2 are not separately bound; they ride `write` unproven.

rows.conformance_note: Canonical CACHE mutation: the offset is derived per-fd state, reconstructible, no governance decision. SEEK_SET/CUR/END/DATA/HOLE, ESPIPE on pipes identical.
Reads derived inode/dentry state; no record. statx mask/attribute semantics identical; /proc metadata reflects gov-os's true derived state (03 §5 note).
probe_limits: statx has no stdlib binding; its extended mask (btime, attributes) rides `stat` unproven.

rows.conformance_note: Derived aggregate; values reflect gov-os's true store.
probe_limits: The binding is statvfs(3), the libc wrapper over statfs(2); the raw struct statfs field layout is not observed. Every field of both is a live figure of the target, so §11.3 makes this shape-only either way.

rows.conformance_note: Evaluates the permission rule (LAW) against current state — a pure query, no state change, no record. R_OK/W_OK/X_OK, AT_EACCESS semantics and errno identical.
probe_limits: access(2) reports through its boolean return, not errno, so §11.1 has nothing to compare on this row; the boolean IS the ABI answer.
Running as root makes every access() answer true; the row is meaningful only on an unprivileged pass and is skipped on a root pass.

rows.what_it_does: Create a hard link (new name for existing inode).
rows.conformance_note: Namespace change — recorded. EEXIST/EMLINK/EXDEV identical.
probe_limits: EXDEV needs two filesystems in one scratch tree and EMLINK needs the link-count ceiling; neither is driven.

rows.conformance_note: Namespace change — recorded (the link is content of a new inode).

rows.what_it_does: Remove a name from the namespace.
rows.conformance_note: Records the name removal. Subtlety: content is content-addressed, so the blob's history persists in the ledger even when the last link drops — but the POSIX contract is exact (link count decremented; space reclaimed when last link gone AND no open fd holds it). AT_REMOVEDIR, EISDIR, ENOTEMPTY identical.
Namespace change — recorded, atomic. RENAME_NOREPLACE/RENAME_EXCHANGE semantics and EEXIST/ENOTEMPTY/EXDEV identical.
probe_limits: renameat2's RENAME_NOREPLACE and RENAME_EXCHANGE have no stdlib binding; they ride `rename` unproven.
EXDEV needs two filesystems in one scratch tree and is not driven.

rows.conformance_note: Namespace create — recorded. EEXIST identical.
Namespace removal — recorded. ENOTEMPTY identical.
Create + (for device nodes) a capability reference — recorded. EPERM on unprivileged device-node creation identical.
probe_limits: mknodat has no stdlib binding; it rides `mknod` unproven.
The successful device-node path needs root; the unprivileged EPERM path is what the map's note names and is what is driven.

rows.conformance_note: Changes content (grow = zero-fill, shrink = drop) — recorded against the content-addressed state. EINVAL/EFBIG identical.
probe_limits: EFBIG needs the filesystem's maximum file size and is not driven.

rows.conformance_note: Space reservation/hole against the storage budget — recorded. FALLOC_FL_* modes and ENOSPC identical.
probe_limits: The binding is posix_fallocate(3), which is mode-0 allocation only; FALLOC_FL_PUNCH_HOLE, _ZERO_RANGE and _COLLAPSE_RANGE have no stdlib binding and are not driven.
ENOSPC needs a full filesystem and is not driven.

rows.conformance_note: The file's permission rule is amended — recorded, cites authority. EPERM on non-owner identical.
probe_limits: EPERM on a non-owned file needs a file owned by another user inside the scratch tree; the harness creates none and does not reach outside its scratch tree to find one, so that errno is not driven.

rows.conformance_note: Ownership/permission amendment — recorded. Set-uid-bit-clear side effect and EPERM identical.
probe_limits: The set-uid-bit-clear side effect needs a successful change of the USER, which needs root; it is not driven on the unprivileged pass.
fchownat has no separate stdlib binding beyond the dir_fd form and is not separately driven.

These steps set the group to gid 4 (adm), which the caller must be a MEMBER of for an unprivileged ownership change to be lawful — a property of the environment a capture runs in, not of the filesystem. A target whose user is not in that group answers EPERM where these captures answer 0, and §11.2a makes that a finding about this ROW rather than about the target. Named here because the row previously drove chown(-1,-1), which changes nothing: the kernel sends no SETATTR, the filesystem is never called, and the row's recording assertion was untestable (design/10 §11.1d; EP-25 ADDENDUM 9 C3).

rows.conformance_note: Metadata mutation recorded; UTIME_NOW/UTIME_OMIT semantics identical.
probe_limits: UTIME_NOW and UTIME_OMIT are not expressible through the stdlib binding (which takes an explicit pair or None-for-now); the OMIT half is not driven.

rows.conformance_note: get/list = CACHE-only read; set/remove = DECISION. Attribute writes are recorded metadata decisions (some xattrs are permission-bearing, e.g. security.*, system.posix_acl_* — those amend permission LAW). ABI and errno identical.
rows.disputed_because: One design/10 row carries two classes on different operations and the note splits it by operation (get/list vs set/remove) but not the permission-bearing sub-case: it says security.* and system.posix_acl_* xattrs 'amend permission LAW' without saying whether those writes are LAW-class or DECISION-class records. The map's words are encoded as written — DECISION for set/remove — and the LAW question is raised rather than decided here.
probe_limits: The security.* and system.posix_acl_* namespaces are not written: they are permission-bearing and writing them needs privilege the unprivileged pass does not have.

rows.conformance_note: Not a governance decision: the writes it commits were already DECISIONS. It is a barrier making the recorded+derived state durable on media. In gov-os the record IS the durability substrate; fsync returns after the covering write-decisions are durable. EIO on flush failure surfaced identically.
probe_limits: EIO on flush failure needs a failing device and is not driven.

rows.conformance_note: As fsync, system-/fs-wide.
probe_limits: syncfs has no stdlib binding; it rides `sync` unproven.

rows.what_it_does: Per-fd control: descriptor flags, status flags, and duplication (F_DUPFD, F_GETFD, F_SETFD, F_GETFL, F_SETFL).
rows.conformance_note: F_DUPFD/F_GETFD/F_SETFD/F_GETFL/F_SETFL = CACHE (fd-table state). All errno identical. [Sub-row of design/10 §6's mixed `fcntl` row, split exactly where that row's own note splits it.]

rows.what_it_does: Per-fd control: query a record lock (F_GETLK).
rows.conformance_note: F_GETLK = CACHE read. [Sub-row of design/10 §6's mixed `fcntl` row, split exactly where that row's own note splits it.]

rows.what_it_does: Per-fd control: take or release a record lock (F_SETLK, F_SETLKW, F_OFD_SETLK).
rows.conformance_note: F_SETLK/F_SETLKW/F_OFD_SETLK = DECISION (a lock grant — recorded, cites rule; a comms coordination event). Blocking-lock wait is a scheduling block/wake. All errno (EAGAIN/EDEADLK) identical. [Sub-row of design/10 §6's mixed `fcntl` row, split exactly where that row's own note splits it.]
probe_limits: EDEADLK needs a deadlock cycle across processes and is not driven.
F_SETLKW's blocking path is a wait, and §11.6 puts timing out of contract; only the non-blocking refusal is driven.

rows.what_it_does: Per-fd control: leases and directory change notification (F_SETLEASE, F_NOTIFY).
rows.conformance_note: F_SETLEASE/F_NOTIFY = DECISION. [Sub-row of design/10 §6's mixed `fcntl` row, split exactly where that row's own note splits it.]
rows.probe_absent_reason: A write lease requires the descriptor to be the file's only opener, which the harness cannot guarantee in a shared scratch tree, and F_NOTIFY is the superseded predecessor of inotify whose delivery is a signal rather than a return value. Neither is driven this EP; the row's assertion exists and its ABI leg is unproven, declared.

rows.conformance_note: Lock grant recorded. LOCK_SH/LOCK_EX/LOCK_NB, EWOULDBLOCK identical.
Adds an fd-table entry to the same open file description — pure cache, no new custody grant. dup2 close-of-target and dup3(O_CLOEXEC) semantics identical.
probe_limits: dup3's O_CLOEXEC form has no stdlib binding; it rides `dup2` unproven.

rows.conformance_note: Reads the dentry-cache-derived listing; no record. On /proc it reads a computed view (§10). Entry order and d_type semantics identical.
probe_limits: Entry ORDER is not asserted: the map promises the d_type semantics and the entry set, and no filesystem promises a directory's on-disk order. The observation is sorted before comparison, which is the guarantee's level (§11.2).

rows.conformance_note: Query.
Per-process cwd is derived state — a cache field mutation; no governance decision. ENOTDIR/EACCES identical.
Query.
probe_limits: Only the final path component is observed: the absolute path contains the scratch root, which differs per target and per run and is therefore a dynamic byte (§11.3).

rows.conformance_note: The files-group involvement in chroot is the path LOOKUP, which is CACHE-only. EPERM on unprivileged identical. [design/10 §11.1f amends §6's table row, which still reads DECISION: chroot(2) changes a PROCESS attribute, a filesystem is consulted for the lookup and never for the root change, and no FUSE filesystem is offered the operation at all. The governance of a process's root re-enters the map with the subsystem that governs process attributes. The §6 sentence this replaces read: 'Recorded confinement decision, cites rule.']
probe_limits: The successful confinement path needs root; on an unprivileged pass the observation is the EPERM the map's own note names. The row's root pass is not built this EP because a successful chroot inside a shared probe process is a confinement the harness would then have to escape.

The row carries no outcome_class and must not gain one. Under design/10 §11.1f it stops expecting a record at all rather than expecting a differently-classed one: declaring NOT-GOVERNED would turn the row green and break the synthetic control fixture, because the fixture produces what the row declares. Reclassifying the row is the amendment; declaring an outcome on an unamended row would have been a way of hiding it (design/10 §11.1f; EP-25 ADDENDUM 10 D1).

What would refute this amendment, stated so a later round can check it cheaply (design/10 §11.1f): if any filesystem interface does receive a root-change notification, the row belongs back in the files group as DECISION and this class is wrong.

rows.conformance_note: Per-process attribute affecting future create decisions; itself derived state. Returns previous mask identically.

rows.what_it_does: Attach a filesystem / configure a new mount.
rows.conformance_note: Mount rules are LAW (§4.3/§4.4) — a recorded, authorized amendment to the namespace. MS_* flags, EBUSY/EPERM identical.
probe_limits: move_mount and the fsopen/fsconfig/fsmount family have no binding built this EP; they ride `mount` unproven.
The MS_* flag matrix (MS_RDONLY, MS_BIND, MS_REC) is not driven: the row's purpose here is the LAW-class assertion and the privileged/unprivileged errno split.

rows.conformance_note: Recorded amendment. MNT_FORCE/MNT_DETACH, EBUSY identical.
probe_limits: MNT_FORCE and MNT_DETACH are not driven; the row drives the plain detach, the not-a-mountpoint errno, and the busy case.

rows.conformance_note: Recorded namespace amendment.
rows.probe_absent_reason: pivot_root needs a prepared new root filesystem and its own mount namespace, and it changes the root of the process that calls it. Driving it means building a second root inside the guest, which is the kernel-entry arc's lab work rather than this instrument's. The row's assertion exists; its ABI leg is unproven, declared.

rows.what_it_does: Copy a range between two files in-kernel.
rows.conformance_note: Destination content recorded (content-addressed; may be a cheap blob-reference clone). Source read is STREAM. Short-copy semantics identical.

rows.what_it_does: Copy from a file fd to another fd.
rows.conformance_note: If destination is a file: a recorded write decision. If a socket: a comms send (DECISION event + STREAM payload). Offset advance and short-transfer semantics identical.
probe_limits: The socket destination is the comms group's population and is driven there, not here.

rows.what_it_does: Move data between fds / pipe buffers with zero copy.
rows.conformance_note: Bulk movement is STREAM traffic; where an endpoint is a durable write or a socket send, that endpoint records its decision. SPLICE_F_* and short-move semantics identical.
probe_limits: tee and vmsplice have no stdlib binding; they ride `splice` unproven.
The SPLICE_F_* flag set is not driven.

rows.what_it_does: Adjust mount attributes / clone a mount tree.
rows.conformance_note: Mount-rule amendments — recorded.
rows.probe_absent_reason: Neither call has a stdlib or libc-wrapper binding, and both take structured arguments (struct mount_attr, OPEN_TREE_CLONE) that a raw binding would have to lay out by hand. Not built this EP; the row's assertion exists and its ABI leg is unproven, declared.
